events.title: Book Launch with Lily Berlin Dodd — In conversation with Misa Sugiura
events.description: We're excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author Lily Berlin Dodd back to the store to celebrate the launch of the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series, The First Flame! Lily will be in conversation with author Misa Sugiura. With Eva locked away in Byrdhaven and Rubi missing, all Dusty can do is avoid capture and (attempt to) sleep through his nightmares in the wake of Cal's death. When fate leads Dusty back to the Lockwood Inn, he overhears the next stage of Eoin Parnassus' sinister plans for aerimanders, and knows he must do everything in his power to stop it. Dodging strict nuns, wanted posters, seasickness, altitude sickness, a clockwork army, and a perilously evil clown on the way, Myrnie, Eva, and Dusty are willing to fight to the ends of the Earth--or at least the edges of their map--to stop Eoin Parnassus, Director of Kingdom Secrets. But Rubi is hiding a shocking truth and Parnassus may pose an even bigger threat than they could ever have imagined. Who can be trusted when secrets lurk around every corner of the Kingdom?
events.blurb: Hear Lily Berlin Dodd talk with author Misa Sugiura about The First Flame, the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series.

events.title: Storytime with Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon
events.description: Join us as we welcome Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon to celebrate their empowering new picture book, No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her journey to finding her voice, independence, and freedom on a skateboard. Kanya Sesser was born without legs, but that doesn't mean she has limits! Sometimes I still fall. But I never give up. I make things work for me. Because I'm strong. Because I'm free. Because I have NO limits. Kanya Sesser has spent her life sharing the message that no matter what life deals you, you can do anything. In this picture book based on her childhood, she tells the story of how she first learned to stand up for herself, both on a skateboard and in life. When people grab her wheelchair to push her to class or onto the bus after school, she's too shocked and too sad to say no. The people around her don't understand that she moves herself. But when she rides a skateboard for the first time, she experiences a new sense of freedom and joy, and she finally finds her voice.
events.blurb: Meet authors Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon at Linden Tree Books and hear their picture book No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her skateboarding journey.

events.title: Storytime with Claire Wrenn Bobrow
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Claire Wrenn Bobrow returns to Linden Tree to share her delightful new picture book, Party Pony! Not another party! Parties used to be Pony's favorite—until every bash turned him into a work horse! Now Pony is a party pooper. How will Pony's friends show him he's worthy of a party too? For any kid who's ever felt left out, this witty picture book is a must-have for the home or school library, and it's perfect for gifting and reading at parties. Grab your copy and join the celebration!
events.blurb: Hear author Claire Wrenn Bobrow read her new picture book, Party Pony!, about a pony who has grown tired of parties.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We hope to introduce interested readers to amazing new books and the opportunity to talk about them in a fun, relaxed group setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Home Scientist (Brownies)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Science is all around us! Brownies begin by making pepper dance using the amazing properties of electricity. Next, they become kitchen chemists and use pantry items to make art with delicious treats. Then they explore properties of density and use them to blow up a balloon without breath and make their own lava lamp. Finally, Brownies will learn how science can be used to make toys and make their very own silly putty! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Home Scientist Badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Make pepper dance with electricity, then use pantry items as a kitchen chemist in this Brownies Home Scientist program.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Tech Detective (Juniors and Cadettes)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Do you have what it takes to be a Tech Detective? Juniors and Cadettes will begin by practicing the art of forensic drawing by sketching a "suspect" as described by a "key witness." Next, they learn about & practice codes and fingerprinting. Juniors will explore the role of DNA in forensics — what it is, what it does, and how it helps solve crimes. They then get to perform an experiment to extract real DNA, and finally use what they have learnt to identify someone from ancient DNA! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Juniors Detective badge or the Cadette Special Agent badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Sketch a "suspect" from a key witness's description, then practice forensic drawing, codes, and fingerprinting as a Junior or Cadette Girl Scout.

events.title: Storytime with Sahar Shams
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Sahar Shams shares her festive debut picture book, What Does Santa Want for Christmas? Every year, children all around the world ask themselves what they'd like to receive from Santa. But one little boy has a different question: What would Santa wish for? Determined, Dorim sets out on a quest to craft the perfect present—but he'll need some help from his friends. With Christmas fast approaching, will they be able to make Santa's wish come true in time?
events.blurb: Hear debut author Sahar Shams read her festive picture book, What Does Santa Want for Christmas?, at a Sunday storytime.

events.venue: Palo Alto Art Center, Meeting Room
events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.

events.title: Vietnamese Storytime & Craft / Kể chuyện và làm thủ công bằng tiếng Việt
events.description: Thân mời các bé cùng cha mẹ hoặc người chăm sóc bé đến tham dự Giờ Kể Chuyện và làm thủ công bằng tiếng Việt tại Thư Viện Evergreen! Chúng ta sẽ cùng nhau nghe kể chuyện, hát ca và tham gia các hoạt động vui nhộn giúp bé phát triển kỹ năng ngôn ngữ và niềm yêu thích đọc sách từ sớm. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Chương trình phù hợp với trẻ em ở mọi độ tuổi và là dịp tuyệt vời để cả gia đình cùng học hỏi, vui chơi và kết nối. Không cần đăng ký trước. Hãy rủ bạn bè cùng tham gia nhé! Join us for a fun and engaging Vietnamese Storytime and Craft at Evergreen Library! Children and their parents or caregivers will enjoy stories, songs, and playful activities in Vietnamese that help build early language and literacy skills. Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! This program is perfect for children of all ages. It's a wonderful opportunity for families to learn, play, and grow together. No registration is required. Bring your friends to join us!
events.attendanceNote: · All participants will need a storytime ticket. Tickets are limited and available at the Information Desk 30 minutes before the program.
events.blurb: Bring your little one to a Vietnamese-language storytime and craft session at Evergreen Library, open to kids with parents or caregivers.

events.title: California Writers Club - South Bay Writers Open Mic
events.description: Are you a writer who would like to read to an audience? Join the South Bay Writers (a chapter of the California Writers Club) for a monthly gathering where anyone may attend and read for up to 10 minutes in any genre. Feedback on your work can be requested from the group, or you can just read! California Writers Club, founded in 1909, is one of the nation's oldest professional clubs for writers. The organization is dedicated to educating writers of all levels and disciplines in the craft of writing and in the marketing of their work. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Read your own writing aloud for up to 10 minutes and get feedback from the California Writers Club at Willow Glen Library.

En este curso práctico aprenderás los fundamentos de la computación, incluyendo el uso del teclado y el mouse, navegación por Internet, correo electrónico, creación de documentos y más. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice speaking English in everyday situations. Learners of all levels are welcome! Free. No registration required.

Mỗi buổi học được hướng dẫn bởi nhân viên thư viện có thể nói được tiếng Việt. Miễn phí. Phải đăng ký và làm bài kiểm tra xếp lớp. events.title: Santa Teresa Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: This leadership and volunteer service group for teens ages 13-18 meets in person on the third Friday of each month from 4-5 PM in the Community Room. Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. Our monthly meetings include: Snacks; Teen volunteer opportunities; Updates on upcoming library teen programs and new materials; Games and activities. events.title: College Readiness
events.description: In this program, get personal assistance with basic college readiness and advice when preparing yourself to further your education. Our knowledgeable volunteer will provide free, one-on-one tutoring at the library. These in-person sessions can help strengthen your knowledge, goals, letter writing, and test-taking skills to improve your college application and set you up for future success! Topics may also include ACT and SAT test prep. Get general high school or college advice on choosing classes, joining clubs, making study plans or setting career goals, networking with teachers or professors, preparing for summer opportunities, and writing resumes or applying for jobs. Get help with general questions about applying to college, application timelines, choosing colleges, essay reviews, and interview practice. Learn what kinds of financial aid are available and how they can help. Please note that no specific financial advice will be given outside of general information and best practices. Space is limited to keep interactions more personalized for each individual. Registration is recommended for a guaranteed spot.

events.blurb: Get free one-on-one tutoring from a volunteer and personal advice on basic college readiness at Seven Trees Library.

events.title: Delphian Lectures: Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties
events.description: The Delphian Study Club presents this lecture series to encourage lifelong learning and friendship. The current series, "Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties," will focus on the history and engineering of musical instruments and the composers who wrote for the instruments. Specific Lecture Topics: September 18, 2026 - Introductory class with series guest lecturer Deborah Rosengaus; October 2, 2026 - Meet the Piano; October 16, 2026 - Meet the Strings; November 6, 2026 - Meet the Guitar; November 20, 2026 - Meet the Brass; December 4, 2026 - Meet the Woodwinds; January 15, 2027 - Meet the Percussion; February 5, 2027 - Meet the Conductors; February 19, 2027 - Meet the Unusual Instruments; March 5, 2027 - Meet the Bach Family; April 2, 2027 - Meet the Mozart Family; April 16, 2027 - Meet the Schumann Family; May 7, 2027 - Meet the Mendelssohn Siblings; May 21, 2027 - Meet the Strauss Family, Waltz Kings. This series will be presented by Deborah Martínez Rosengaus, a versatile mezzo-soprano who has studied opera, theater, music and dance, and has toured internationally with a variety of musical ensembles in concert halls such as Suntory Hall in Tokyo, The Center for Performing Arts in Beijing, Disney Hall with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, The Lincoln Center and Carnegie Hall. She has given recitals in Mexico and across the United States, giving voice to her research into the lesser-known art songs of great classical composers. Ms. Rosengaus holds a Master of Music degree from the Manhattan School of Music, where she studied with international opera diva Mignon Dunn, and a bachelor's degree from the University of Southern California Thornton School of Music. She is the recipient of several awards including the Schoenfeld Award from the Holt Memorial Scholarship Competition and 1st place in the Pacific Musical Society Competition. She has also performed in master classes with Karen Morrow and Luana Devol, and is a featured vocalist on several independent film soundtracks. She is known for her exciting, high-energy performances and for creating memorable and endearing characters such as the role of Principessa Louling under the baton of Bruno Riggacci in the world premiere of his one-act opera "Dodici personaggi in cerca di voce." She has received critical acclaim for her interpretation of Jo in Mark Adamo's Little Women and was nominated for a Theater Bay Area Award for the role of Ruth in Pirates of Penzance. Guests are always welcome and encouraged. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Hear a Delphian Study Club lecture titled Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties at Willow Glen Library on a Friday morning.

events.title: The GreenRoots Collective: Environmental Technology Workshops
events.description: Discover how science and engineering can be used to understand and solve real environmental challenges. In this hands-on GreenRoots Collective workshop series, students will explore sustainability through interactive experiments, engineering challenges, collaborative problem-solving, and community-focused projects. Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important part of the world students are growing up in. Understanding how the environment works, and how everyday decisions, technology, and engineering can help protect it, gives young learners the tools to think critically about real-world problems and envision better solutions for the future. Rather than simply learning environmental concepts, students will put them into practice. Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution. Students will also contribute to community projects that connect their learning to meaningful action beyond the classroom. Through the program, participants will strengthen scientific reasoning, engineering design, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills while developing a deeper understanding of sustainability and how STEM can be used to create positive change. Series Topics: 1. Floodproof! The Science & Engineering of El Niño - November 8; 2. Cooler Cities: Engineering Solutions to Urban Heat - November 20; 3. Clean Air Lab: The Science of Pollution & Filtration - December 13; 4. Microplastics Lab: Investigating Tiny Plastics in Our Environment - December 18. Ages: 7-12. Registration recommended!
events.blurb: Learn how science and engineering help understand and solve environmental challenges in a GreenRoots Collective workshop at Seven Trees Library.

events.title: Beyond the Spotlight: One Life. Multiple Passions. Endless Possibilities
events.description: In this inspiring talk with professionals, we explore how passion for the performing arts can coexist with a primary career. Can you be a professional by day and a performer by choice? What does it look like when theater becomes more than a hobby without becoming your full-time profession? Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like. We will discuss how aspiring performers can balance education, professional goals, personal responsibilities, and their love for the stage. Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on pursuing Performing Arts and Theater as a Parallel Career Path: an exploration of passion, purpose, possibility, and the courage to embrace more than one professional identity. Carla Pantoja: Carla, born and raised in the South Bay, is an actor, fight director, teaching artist, intimacy director, and mom of two. She has been a Resident Artist of San Francisco Shakespeare Festival since 2014 and recently served as Director of Vision for the 2021 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Pericles, Prince of Tyre, directing episodes 2 and 4. In 2020, she was in the acting company at Oregon Shakespeare Festival, returning in 2022 as the festival's first female fight director. Carla is an associate instructor for Dueling Arts International and serves on their governing body as President. She is also a proud member of Making Good Trouble, an anti-racist training cohort based in the Bay Area. Carla has directed SF Shakes' Shakespeare on Tour productions of Romeo and Juliet and Comedy of Errors and assistant-directed the 2017 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Hamlet. She played Paulina in Free Shakespeare in the Park's The Winter's Tale, Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, and Kate in The Taming of the Shrew. She's performed with Cal Shakes, Shotgun Players, Crowded Fire, Playground, Lorraine Hansberry Theatre, and the SF Mime Troupe in the Bay Area, to name a few. Vinay Pande: Vinay Pande is a Silicon Valley technology leader and a passionate theatre artist who brings together the worlds of innovation and performing arts. Originally from Mumbai, India, Vinay holds a degree in Instrumentation Engineering and began his career in telecommunications, where he was part of the core team that developed India's first satellite-based mission-critical voice, data, and video network for the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). He later worked as a researcher at the prestigious Bell Labs, holds 15 technology patents, and has co-authored technical publications and books. Today, he serves as a Principal Architect at a leading technology company in Silicon Valley. Beyond his technology career, Vinay has nurtured a deep passion for the performing arts for over a decade, actively pursuing theatre, acting, and singing across Marathi and Hindi productions. From bringing diverse characters to life on stage to engaging audiences as a Radio Jockey and event host, he thrives on the energy of live performance and the magic of storytelling. For Vinay, technology may be his profession, but the stage is where his creative spirit truly comes alive. Sowmya Renukuntla: Sowmya is a Bay Area native and recent graduate from Santa Clara University, where she studied Business and worked directly with Admission Counselors for four years. Since graduating, she has been working full-time at Levi Strauss & Co. on the Corporate Insights team and is a part-time college counselor. Sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation. events.title: Everyone Can Create: Let's Create a Beat! Using GarageBand

events.title: 3D Printing One-on-One Appointment
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Do you have a 3D design or project but don't have a 3D printer and/or need help printing your design? If so, the West Valley Branch Library invites you to register for a two-hour appointment where a volunteer will help you print your project on the library's 3D printer. Appointments are scheduled on the first and third Saturdays of each month from 12:30-2:30. During the appointment, you will learn how to set up a file and print your design with guidance from one of our volunteers. Registered participants can choose a design from Thingiverse, Printables, or provide their own design. Designs must be in .stl format and will be printed with PLA filament. Your .stl file (or a link to your .stl file on Thingiverse or Printables) must be submitted via email to wvmail@sjlibrary.org no later than the Thursday before your appointment. All prints are free and must meet the criteria listed below. Registration is required. Only 1 print per person and only 1 print per family/household per month. Also, please be aware that: Designs must be able to be loaded and saved on a Creality K1C 3D printer. All prints must take less than 1 hr 30 min (estimated 60 grams of filament). Prints are meant to be for personal use only and not for commercial purposes. No weapons or items that could be construed as a weapon will be accepted for print. Prints that are considered obscene or otherwise inappropriate for the library environment will not be accepted for printing. The library's 3D printers must be used only for lawful purposes. All local, state, and federal laws must be followed. Accepted prints may not violate any third party's intellectual property, such as copyright, patent, or trademark. SJPL and library staff are not responsible for malfunctions or misprints. Library staff reserve the right to refuse any 3D print request.
events.blurb: Print your own 3D design on the library's printer during a two-hour appointment with a volunteer helping you through it.

events.title: ARTrepreneurs: Teen Craft Fair
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Looking for cute, fun, creative, and crafty wares? Check out the ARTrepreneur: Teen Craft Fair. All teens featured at this fair have completed the ARTrepreneur program and are small business owners. Come support them and check out their incredible products. Cash and most payment apps accepted. No obligation to purchase. The fair takes place during the TeenHQ Theater Production. Fuzzy and Fluffy is among the scheduled vendors and will sell popular crocheted items, including loaf cats, octopi, and chickens. Its keychains include mini octopuses, mushroom pops, and mini chickens. These items are perfect as birthday or holiday gifts, or even room decor! We're looking forward to meeting you at our market! Welcome to Green Apple Boutique! We are a small business located in the Bay Area and would love to have you as a part of our community! Our shop is currently focusing on the production of pins and jewelry but we plan to expand our inventory to cute stationery in the future! Lils Creations features handmade jewelry, customized stationery, beadable pens, unique keychains and charms. Designed with care, high-quality materials, and a touch of character-inspired charm, my items are crafted to offer thoughtful, one-of-a-kind gifts and accessories. Calderon & Co's business is the amalgamation of a love for toys, 3D printing, and making money. The goal was to create a toy that could satisfy the urge to fidget or imagine new things, staving off the spontaneous horrors of a bored mind, without being a traditional, hyper-consumeristic toy that serves little purpose beyond draining your wallet. Three main problems were identified, alongside a single solution: affordable toys suck, they don't keep people still, and the CEO of C&C is very broke. The solution? A selection of 3D-printed fidget toys, tested profusely. What makes this selection unique is that people of all ages can come to the table and try the fidgets firsthand. Every effort is made to ensure product quality through careful selection of what gets sold, and by personally breaking them in so the initial rough texture is ameliorated as much as possible. Aydraw Art makes practical trinkets such as beautiful handmade keychains, pipe cleaner flowers, cards, cups, jewelry bowls, and more to inspire your creativity! For reasonable prices, add some bling and express your individuality and creativity today! Two Tiny Potatoes sells yarn-crafted items including star wands, keychains, flower hair clips, arm cuffs, coasters, and hand warmers. Forever Flowers blends the beauty of bouquets with everlasting love from crocheting, which makes it the perfect gift for yourself or others to commemorate a moment with. Forever Flowers offers a wide range of crocheted products including flowers, coasters, and plants. At Earthwise Pens, we believe in being as environmentally friendly as possible, without making the product expensive. Our products have the same level of quality as other products, and the same price, but eco-friendly. Meghna's Nails sells handmade press-on nails. Each set is carefully painted with gel polish, beads, and gems. We bring affordable and convenient nails that are available in a variety of designs, shapes, and sizes straight to you! Great for elevating any outfit, Meghna's Nails brings beauty to the details! Learn about the ARTrepreneur program and how teens bring their small business dreams to life. Celebrating 10 years of SJPL TeenHQ.

Participants may receive a 3D-printed giveaway for taking part. Basic computer familiarity required (no prior 3D design experience needed). Please make sure to create an account on Tinkercad before class starts if you don't already have one. Parents need to stay with their children if the children do not have/know their username and password for Tinkercad. Computers and space are limited. You are welcome to bring your own laptop. Registration required: Please only register if you plan to attend. If you are unable to attend, please be sure to cancel your registration at least 24 hours in advance, giving staff time to contact people on the waitlist.

events.description: This November, children in kindergarten to second grade are invited to participate in hands-on science experiments alongside their parents and caregivers. These programs are designed to be self-paced and child-led. Accompanying adults are expected to facilitate the experiments and activities for their children. Conduct a new experiment each Sunday! November 1st: The Lost Key – Magnets and Magnetism; November 8th: The Redwoods – Redwood Trees and their Roots; November 15th: A House for Bear – Building Materials and their Properties; November 22nd: The Wilted Plant – Plants and Capillary Action; November 29th: Sound – Vibrations and Sound. Registration is required for each program. Extra science kits will be available at the reference desk after each program concludes. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes.
events.blurb: Draw with pencils in timed rounds of 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute, in a one-hour figure-drawing workshop.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng

Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. This free, noncredit course, ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1, is for high-beginning English learners. It focuses on basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026; Ends: December 10, 2026; Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday; Time: 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM; Instructor: Michelle N. Henninger. Before the classes start, you must complete a Guided Self-Placement (GSP). This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.
events.blurb: Write your name in Hangul using calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper in a 90-minute workshop.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: We'll be reading Elatsoe by Darcie Little Badger in honor of Native American Heritage Month. Sign up at the adult reference desk to get a copy. "Imagine an America very similar to our own. It's got homework, best friends, and pistachio ice cream. There are some differences. This America has been shaped dramatically by the magic, monsters, knowledge, and legends of its peoples, those Indigenous and those not. Some of these forces are charmingly everyday, like the ability to make an orb of light appear or travel across the world through rings of fungi. But other forces are less charming and should never see the light of day. Seventeen-year-old Elatsoe ("Ellie" for short) lives in this slightly stranger America. She can raise the ghosts of dead animals, a skill passed down through generations of her Lipan Apache family. Her beloved cousin has just been murdered, in a town that wants no prying eyes. But she is going to do more than pry. The picture-perfect façade of Willowbee masks gruesome secrets, and she will rely on her wits, skills, and friends to tear off the mask and protect her family." For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.description: The Plot Thickens Mystery Book Discussion: Hercule Poirot's Christmas by Agatha Christie (1938). A family reunion at Christmas time should suggest family warmth and seasonal merriment. When the tyrannical millionaire Simeon Lee commands his four sons to join him at his country estate for Christmas, Hercule Poirot finds himself trying to solve the mystery of his host's murder, instead. After Lee alienates each of his sons with barbed insults and announces he's planning to change his will, all four of them have a motive to want their father dead. The Plot Thickens Mystery Book Discussion meets on the first Wednesday of even months at 11 am in Room 201B. All adults who love to read and discuss mysteries are welcome. events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never-before-seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film, including KQED, but national PBS has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers. Registration is not required, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Watch a screening of The Panama Deception, a documentary on the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama and its aftermath.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces
events.description: Are you experiencing the "holiday guest stress syndrome"? Don't let the pressure of having a perfect tablescape wilt your holiday spirit! Join UC Master Gardeners Laura Westley, Sue Neufeld, and Bernie Day for an inspiring, hands-on demonstration designed to take the stress—and the high cost—out of holiday decorating. You don't need a professional florist or a massive budget to create a "wow" factor for your dining room. What You'll Learn: The Art of the "Found" Object: Learn how to scout your own backyard or junk drawer for unique textures, greenery, and accents that add character to any arrangement. Grocery Store Glam: Discover how to deconstruct those affordable supermarket flower bunches and reimagine them into high-end-looking centerpieces. Pro-Tips for Longevity: Get the inside scoop on keeping your flora fresh from the first toast to the final slice of pie. Why join us? Whether you're hosting a grand feast or an intimate gathering, you'll walk away with the confidence and practical skills to transform "ordinary" items into extraordinary focal points. events.title: CNPS Talk #3: The birds, the bees, and a magic trait: The evolution of red hummingbird flowers in California, a talk by Prof. Justen Whittall
events.description: Why are so many of California's favorite hummingbird flowers red? From California fuchsia blooming in the fall to western columbine, scarlet bugler, and Indian paintbrush, our native flora is full of brilliant red flowers that hummingbirds love. But is red simply a color that attracts hummingbirds, or does it also help flowers avoid unwanted visits from bees? Join Santa Clara University biology professor Justen Whittall to explore how hummingbirds and bees see flowers differently, including a hidden world of ultraviolet colors invisible to humans. Drawing on recent research with his students and international collaborators, he'll reveal how these hidden pigments may help explain not only why hummingbird flowers are red, but also how new plant species evolve. Speaker Biography: Justen Whittall was born in Santa Clara and earned his B.S. in Biology from Santa Clara University, an M.S. from Oregon State University studying monkeyflower conservation genetics, and a Ph.D. from UC Santa Barbara investigating the evolution of California columbines. Following postdoctoral research at UC Davis on the evolution of California's serpentine-endemic plants, including blue-eyed Mary, wallflowers, and jewelflowers, he returned to SCU in 2007 as a professor of Biology. He works closely with undergraduates to uncover the mysteries of plant ecology and evolution, with research ranging from the conservation of rare Santa Clara County plants—including jewelflowers, columbines, liveforevers, and Hoita—to the evolution of flower color and hummingbird pollination in California's native flora. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Discuss Michael Chabon's The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay with fellow readers at the Pageturners book group.

events.title: Non-Fiction Book Discussion – Finders Keepers: a Tale of Archaeological Plunder and Obsession
events.description: In December, the Cupertino Library's nonfiction book group will discuss Craig Childs' 2010 book Finders Keepers: A Tale of Archaeological Plunder and Obsession. Journalist Craig Childs documents his efforts to find and preserve precious and ancient artifacts from the American Southwest that could help answer questions about the people who made and used them. From archaeological digs in the deserts of Arizona and New Mexico to high-end art galleries and museums in New York and Boston, Childs had to protect the artifacts and himself from ruthless art smugglers, risking his life and freedom multiple times. Childs' book also asks who owns the past and its archaeological finds. An archaeologist may be praised for excavating an ancient site and sharing their finds with a famous museum. Someone who takes a precious relic from a museum because they believe it is sacred and belongs where it was found is called a thief. Which one is in the wrong? The Non-fiction Book Discussion group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am. All meetings are held in Room 201B. Sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Celebrating Yalda Night
events.description: Join us for a special Yalda Night celebration with children's author Anahita Tamaddon and a reading of her book, Yalda Night! Experience the beauty of this cherished Persian tradition through a Yalda-inspired story, music, and a fun paper craft featuring one of Yalda's beloved symbols. Yalda, the longest night of the year, is a joyful celebration of family, storytelling, and togetherness as we welcome the arrival of winter. All craft materials will be provided. Children ages three and up, along with their adult caregivers, are invited to participate. Materials will be available while supplies last. While registration isn't required and doesn't guarantee a spot, it is recommended if you'd like a reminder about the event. برای جشن ویژه‌ی شب یلدا همراه با نویسنده‌ی کتاب‌های کودک، آناهیتا تمدن، به ما بپیوندید. در این برنامه با زیبایی‌های این سنت دیرینه‌ی ایرانی از طریق قصه‌ای با حال‌وهوای یلدا، موسیقی و ساخت کاردستی کاغذی با الهام از یکی از نمادهای دوست‌داشتنی یلدا آشنا خواهیم شد. شب یلدا، بلندترین شب سال، فرصتی برای جشن گرفتن در کنار خانواده و عزیزان، قصه‌گویی و با هم بودن و همچنین خوشامدگویی به فصل زمستان است. تمام وسایل مورد نیاز برای ساخت کاردستی فراهم خواهد بود.
events.blurb: Hear author Anahita Tamaddon read her book Yalda Night and make a Yalda-inspired paper craft.

events.title: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Sit for guided sitting and releasing meditation with Phuong Pham, then join a group sharing and Q&A session.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: NeuroSphere: Neuroscience and More!
events.description: Come join the teen-led group NeuroSphere! This session will dive into the basics of brain function, fun activities to test your brainpower, and an introduction to future career opportunities. There will be snacks; feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through NeuroSphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com.
events.blurb: Join teen-led NeuroSphere to dig into brain function basics and test your brainpower with hands-on activities.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: Double Play on the Red Line with Raj Oza
events.description: Join us for a special discussion with local author Raj Oza about his book Double Play on the Red Line. Here's a chance to talk to a writer about his writing process and to hear how he came to write this novel. Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Talk with local author Raj Oza about Double Play on the Red Line and hear how he came to write the novel.

events.title: Learn English: Beyond the Basics
events.description: The 8-week, in-person English as a Second Language (ESL) class covers grammar, pronunciation, and idioms. The class is for intermediate and advanced English learners ages 18 and older who can have a conversation in English and want to improve their pronunciation and understanding. Register once for the full 8-week series and double-check your email address. Registration closes in the 3rd week. You may lose your spot if you miss the 1st class. If you cannot attend the 1st class, please email Priya Murthy at priya.murthy@paloalto.gov.
events.blurb: Practice English grammar, pronunciation, and idioms in an in-person ESL class that meets Friday at midday.

events.title: Open Sewing Studio
events.description: Do you have a sewing project but need the equipment and space? Are you interested in learning about the basics of a sewing machine? Open Sewing Studio is a space for both beginners looking to learn as well as experienced sewists looking for the time and space to work on their project. We will have sewing machines, table space, fabric scraps, and tools available for attendees. Bring your own projects and have fun! Note: Teens and adults only. Use of machines will be on a first-come, first-served basis due to limited supply. Our staff is only available to support very basic projects. Please keep in mind Open Sewing Studio is limited to 1.5 hours.

events.title: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Sit for guided sitting and releasing meditation with Phuong Pham, then join a group sharing and Q&A session.

events.title: TLAB presents: The Brave Fuzzy Author Talk
events.description: Ever wondered how to blend creative writing with the wonders of science? Join us for an interactive afternoon with the authors behind The Brave Fuzzy. Members of Pen & Pipette, a nonprofit publisher for children's books run entirely by high school students, will share what inspired the book, explore how art and science come together, and lead a hands-on workshop where you can experiment with your own creative ideas. Perfect for curious minds, aspiring writers, and science lovers alike.
events.blurb: Meet the authors behind The Brave Fuzzy and learn how creative writing and science can blend together in an interactive talk.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Join the Pageturners book group for an evening discussion of nonfiction, fiction and biography at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Big Bunny 5K and Kids Fun Run
events.address: Cupertino Civic Center, 10300 Torre Avenue, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Lace up and join the fun at the Big Bunny 5K! Run, walk, or hop your way through a 3.1-mile course winding through the streets of Cupertino, starting and finishing at the Cupertino Civic Center. Whether you're racing for a personal best or enjoying a morning out with friends and family, this community fun run is the perfect way to kick off the day. For our youngest participants (ages 7 and under), we offer a special kid-friendly course on Library Field—short, sweet, and designed for maximum fun. Everyone who participates is a winner!
events.costNote: Kids’ run $30–$35. 5K $47–$60 depending on registration date and residency.
events.attendanceNote: The 5K starts at 8:30 AM by Community Hall and costs $47–$60. The kids’ run starts at 9:30 AM on Library Field for ages 7 and under and costs $30–$35. Same-day registration runs from 7 to 8:15 AM at Community Hall.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Join us for a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. Music & Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.

events.title: Math Club
events.description: Improve your math skills and apply them through fun math-related activities! Participants will focus on a variety of math concepts and do hands-on math activities in this weekly drop-in program. For children in grades 3-5 only. Registration not required. Instruction on the week's concept will occur during the first 15-20 minutes, so please arrive on time. This program meets in person during the school year. We may cancel some meetings due to school/holiday breaks or volunteer unavailability.
events.blurb: Tackle hands-on math activities and concepts each week in this drop-in club for grades 3-5.

events.description: Are you a student in grades K-6 who needs help with homework? Trained tutors offer free homework help every Tuesday and Thursday from 4:30 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. No registration is required. Basic school supplies will be provided. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Thread & Tea Society
events.description: Come join our fiber craft society! Work on your own project, start something new, or learn the basics with help from our knowledgeable volunteer. Bring your knitting, crochet, embroidery, felting, or another fiber arts project. It's a relaxed, creative space to build skills and connect with fellow makers of all ages. Hooks, needles, yarn, and basic supplies provided while supplies last. The program is for ages 8 and up. Younger children are welcome with adult supervision. All skill levels welcome.
events.blurb: Knit, crochet, embroider, or work with felt on your own project, or learn the basics from a volunteer.

events.title: Fiber Arts Circle
events.description: Do you enjoy crocheting or knitting? Want to see what others are working on, refine your skills, or connect with other crafters? Grab your project and join us every week in the Almaden Library living room (behind the Tech Center where the newspapers and magazines are kept) to crochet or knit (or embroider or tat or...) and chat with other crafters making things with yarn. All hand needle crafts welcome. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Branch Library.
events.blurb: Bring your crochet or knitting project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the library's living room.

events.title: Earth and Arbor Day Festival
events.description: Cupertino's annual Earth and Arbor Day Festival is an interactive event that invites community members of all ages to learn about environmental issues and solutions in a family-friendly atmosphere. Explore booths, hands-on activities, live entertainment, and food trucks. Connect with local organizations working to protect our environment at this free community event. For additional information on the City's Earth and Arbor Day festival, see the Earth and Arbor Day Festival webpage.
events.blurb: Learn about environmental issues and solutions at Cupertino's annual festival, with interactive activities for all ages.

events.title: Holiday Jazz Music
events.description: Join us for MAK Band Jazz, a special sing-along performance of holiday favorites. This band is an ensemble featuring guitar, ukulele, trumpet, tenor saxophone, alto saxophone, clarinet, trombone, bass, drums, harmonica and percussion, along with special guest jazz musicians. They will perform popular holiday music, including songs such as "Jingle Bells," "Frosty the Snowman," "Let It Snow," "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree," and others. This is a family program. All are welcome.
events.blurb: Sing along to holiday favorites with MAK Band Jazz, an ensemble of guitar, ukulele, horns, clarinet, bass, drums and harmonica.

events.title: Music and Movement
events.description: Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Free. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Sing songs, trade rhymes, and move along with early literacy activities built for families with kids of mixed ages.

events.title: Enlightened: Visible Light STEM Workshop
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Welcome to Enlightened, a visible light workshop for kids 10 and under! The workshop includes 3 activities that encourage curiosity about light. Participants will create personalized prints using cyanotype paper and make their very own kaleidoscope. Join us to get your shine on! Free. No registration required. Recommended for elementary school students with adult supervision. Presented by teen volunteers in Girls Empowered in Math and Science (GEMS).
events.blurb: Make cyanotype prints and your own kaleidoscope in a visible light workshop for kids 10 and under.

events.title: A Look into the Night Sky with Astro Everywhere
events.description: Join us at the Children's Library for a special evening of astronomy with Astro Everywhere! We'll gather in the Treetop Room for a live astronomy show featuring planetarium software to explore the night sky as seen from Palo Alto. Then, head to the Secret Garden for a telescope demonstration and a closer look at the Moon and Saturn. We'll wrap up the evening with a cozy cup of hot cocoa! Thank you to the Friends of the Palo Alto Library (FOPAL) for their generous support.
events.blurb: Watch a live astronomy show in the Treetop Room, using planetarium software to see the night sky as it appears over Palo Alto.

events.title: Tutoring Kidz
events.description: Join us for a fun and exciting tutoring program led by two high school students, Addison and Sarah! Their goal is to make learning an enjoyable and rewarding experience for every student. Through engaging games, creative activities, and interactive lessons, they help students strengthen their English and math skills while building confidence and discovering the joy of learning. Come learn, play, and succeed! Perfect for children ages 5–12! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Work through tutoring sessions led by two high school students, Addison and Sarah, who aim to make learning enjoyable.

events.title: Teen Resource Fair

events.description: This event is focused on helping teens explore City of Cupertino summer job opportunities and volunteer programs that build real-world skills and look great on college and job applications. events.title: Community Threads: Lunar New Year Felt Goat
events.description: It's the year of the goat! In this workshop, folks will make a felt goat for Lunar New Year. We will only be hand sewing in this workshop. Open to teens and adults only. The workshop is suitable for the advanced beginner, intermediate, or advanced sewist. Knowledge of hand sewing and the sewing machine is required. You should know how to thread the machine, fill the bobbin, and use the backstitch, and you should understand the various other parts and functions of the sewing machine.

All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome!

Storytime includes a variety of early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is targeted to children under the age of two and their caregivers.
