events.title: Cupertino Spelling Bee
events.address: Cupertino Community Hall, 10350 Torre Ave, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: The Cupertino Spelling Bee is an annual contest for Cupertino students in grades 2-5, and is organized by the Cupertino Parks and Recreation Department and the Cupertino Youth Activity Board. Please note: The Cupertino Spelling Bee is not affiliated with the National Scripps Spelling Bee and we cannot sponsor or send winners to the National Spelling Bee. Registration will open with winter activity registration.
events.blurb: Watch Cupertino students in grades 2 to 5 compete in the annual spelling bee run by Parks and Recreation and the Youth Activity Board.

events.title: Bilingual Family Storytime
events.description: This 30-minute storytime features movement, singing, and action! The early literacy focus is on sharing stories and songs in English and Mandarin Chinese. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Sing, move, and hear stories in English and Mandarin during this 30-minute evening storytime.

events.title: Community Threads: Holiday Placemat
events.description: In this workshop, folks will learn how to make a festive holiday placemat to decorate their homes for the holidays. The workshop is suitable for the advanced beginner, intermediate, or advanced sewist. Knowledge of the sewing machine is required. You should know how to thread the machine, fill the bobbin, and use the backstitch, and you should understand the various other parts and functions of the sewing machine. Open to teens and adults only.
events.blurb: Sew a festive holiday placemat in this workshop for advanced beginner to advanced sewists.

events.title: Sunday STEAM
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Drop in every fourth Sunday at 1 PM for a new hands-on STEAM activity in robotics, engineering, or science. Supplies will be provided but may be limited and will be available while they last. For November, we will make a wearable DIY Robotic Hand using cardboard, straws, hot glue guns, and more. Free. This activity will use hot glue guns. We will have supplies for about 20 participants. No registration required.
events.blurb: Drop in to explore robotics, engineering, or science through hands-on projects. Supplies are available while they last.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interactions with our reading volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading aloud with our volunteer. Please note: this is not a tutoring session. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Meet a reading volunteer for one-on-one or small group storytime and practice reading aloud yourself.

events.title: Art of Living Meditation
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Why wait to find greater peace in your life? Join volunteers from the Art of Living Foundation every Sat. morning at 11:00 AM for a relaxing meditation session. Sessions will include simple yoga stretches that can be done sitting on a chair, calming breathing techniques (pranayama), and a guided meditation. Art of Living volunteers will be available after the meditation to answer questions. Beginners are welcome.
events.blurb: Join Art of Living Foundation volunteers for a Saturday morning meditation session at the library.

events.title: Saturday Board Games Day
events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. Attendees can bring their own games to play or jump in with others. Please bring your own snacks and drinks to fuel an afternoon of marathon gaming in the El Camino Room. Presented by The Bay Area Boardgames Meetup Group. Masks are not required in the Palo Alto Libraries, but are recommended.
events.blurb: Play modern board games at Downtown Library, bringing your own or joining a table with other gamers during the day-long meetup.

events.title: Tech Mentor
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Need help printing or using Word and Excel? Want to set up an email account? Need ideas on tech security? Questions about accessing SJPL e-resources? From the basics to somewhat beyond, volunteer tech mentors are here to help with thoughtful advice and problem-solving. We will do our best to assist you with your tech dilemmas. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Bring your questions on printing, Word, Excel, email setup, or tech security to volunteer tech mentors who offer advice and problem-solving.

events.title: LEGO Spike Robots!
events.description: Learn basic engineering and coding while having LEGO-style fun with LEGO Spike Prime! Participants will follow simple step-by-step picture instructions on a tablet to build an exciting frog, dog, or other kind of robot, and then learn to use simple Word Blocks to make their robot perform their commands! This program is great for beginners. No prior experience is necessary. Limited to 10 participants. Free.
events.blurb: Build and code LEGO Spike Prime robots while picking up basic engineering skills at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Neighborhood Hands Bi-monthly Cleanup
events.description: Our pilot program meets every other Saturday at 7:45 a.m. in Guadalupe Gardens just north of the Spring St. cul-de-sac off Coleman Avenue across from Target. (Google Maps directions here; see red pin on map below.) If the weather is good, we clean the park until approximately 9:15 a.m.; unhoused neighbors receive stipends, and then everyone enjoys a vibrant and growing community resource fair until ~10:30 a.m.
events.blurb: Help clean Guadalupe Gardens, then stay for the community resource fair.

events.title: STEM: Make Fake Snow
events.description: Use simple science to make fake snow with support from Lynbrook High WiSTEM. All ages welcome. While supplies last. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Use simple science to make fake snow with Lynbrook High WiSTEM at Saratoga Library. All ages are welcome.

events.title: Children's Area Scavenger Hunts
events.description: Pick up a checklist at the table in the Children's Area. Look for the images around the Children's Area. Once you have found all of the images on the checklist, come to the table in the Children's Area for a prize while supplies last. Themes vary each week. Free. No registration required. This will take place in the Children's Area from 1 PM-2 PM. No scavenger hunt on 11/07/2026.
events.blurb: Grab a checklist and hunt for hidden images around the Children's Area to win a small prize.

events.title: STEM November
events.description: Join us in the evening for a STEM activity during the Thanksgiving School Break. Monday, November 23: Buzz Off. Tuesday, November 24: Hovercraft. Wednesday, November 25: Stop Motion Animation. Free, with limited capacity. No registration required. Appropriate for ages 8-12. The sign-in sheet is available at the information desk 30 minutes before the program starts. Everyone who attends must sign in.
events.blurb: Try hands-on STEM activities during Thanksgiving break, from Buzz Off to hovercrafts to stop motion animation, for ages 8-12, free and drop-in.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One-on-One Computer Help
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as printing, using email, connecting to Wi-Fi, creating documents, and accessing library resources such as e-books. We can also provide basic instructions for using devices such as laptops, smartphones, e-readers, etc. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Get personalized help with email, printing, Wi-Fi, and more at this Monday tech session.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club: Beginning
events.description: Come practice English with us! Learners will study everyday vocabulary and basic listening and speaking skills. Suitable for beginning English learners. Free. Registration required. ¡Ven a practicar inglés con nosotros! Los estudiantes aprenderán vocabulario común y habilidades básicas de conversación. Adecuado para estudiantes de inglés de nivel principiante. Gratis. Es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Practice everyday vocabulary and basic listening and speaking skills in a free conversation club for beginning English learners; registration is required.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club
events.description: The ESL Conversation Club is returning to the Milpitas Library! Please join us for this fun sharing experience. Improve your English listening and speaking skills and learn about other cultures in a supportive environment. This program is for adults aged 18 and older who speak basic English. We will be holding ongoing weekly meetings in the Program Room on the first floor. We welcome drop-ins!
events.blurb: Practice English listening and speaking with other learners and hear about different cultures at the Milpitas Library conversation club.

events.title: Berryessa Book Club
events.description: Join the Berryessa Book Club on the third Friday of each month for a fun, engaging literary discussion. In November, which is National Native American Heritage Month, we will read There There by Tommy Orange. The book explores themes of Native peoples living in urban spaces and the ambivalence and complexity of Natives' struggles with identity and authenticity. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Join a literary discussion of Tommy Orange's There There with the Berryessa Book Club on a Friday afternoon.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Bring your dancing feet to the Mitchell Park Library on Wednesday evenings for Music & Movement with Librarian Celina. Build early literacy skills through movement, songs, and dance. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. This program is meant for families with children, and no previous experience is needed!
events.blurb: Dance, sing, and play instruments with Librarian Celina at Mitchell Park Library's Music & Movement session.

events.title: Wee Love Art: Frida Kahlo
events.description: Celebrate creativity and explore the vibrant legacy of Frida Kahlo, a pioneering Mexican artist, with our Wee Love Art program. Immerse yourself in Kahlo's colorful world of self-expression and symbolism through hands-on art activities inspired by her iconic style. Join us on this artistic journey as we honor the life and legacy of this extraordinary artist. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Make hands-on art inspired by Frida Kahlo's style at this Wee Love Art session at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Digital Skills: Zoom
events.description: Build your confidence with technology in this hands-on workshop. Get step-by-step guidance on how to join or host a Zoom meeting using video, phone, or chat. The workshop takes place on the 1st and 3rd Fridays in November: Friday, November 6th, 4:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m.; Friday, November 20th, 4:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. The presenters can speak Vietnamese and Hindi. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn how to join or host a Zoom meeting by video, phone, or chat in a hands-on workshop with step-by-step guidance.

events.title: Live Well Age Well Health Expo
events.address: Cupertino Senior Center, 21251 Stevens Creek Blvd, 95014
events.description: Embrace a vibrant life at 50 and beyond! Join the Cupertino Senior Center for the Live Well Age Well Health Expo designed for individuals ages 50 and better. Explore booths, resources, and educational sessions tailored to support a healthy lifestyle as you age. Then get moving with exciting activity demonstrations, perfect for discovering new exercises that will help you stay active!
events.blurb: Browse health booths and resources, and sit in on educational sessions at the Cupertino Senior Center's expo for people ages 50 and better.

These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.

events.title: Guided Meditation & Yoga for Wellness and Stress Relief

Presented by Dhyan Foundation, dedicated to promoting physical, mental and spiritual well-being through authentic yogic practices and community education.
events.blurb: Try guided meditation and simple standing or chair-based stretches led by the Dhyan Foundation.

Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer. The program will be held under the Read to Children sign within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Join a volunteer for a small-group reading session in Berryessa Library's Children's Area.

This program is generously sponsored by the Pearl Avenue Friends of the Library.
events.blurb: Make a foldable sunflower fan at Pearl Avenue Library. Supplies are provided, and the program is free with no registration required.

events.title: Jewelry Making for Adults
events.description: Get crafty and relax at a jewelry-making night just for adults. Supplies will be available to create whatever you like. Make something for yourself or a gift for a friend. Better yet, bring a friend! Not sure where to start? We'll have project ideas and examples to help you get inspired. Come be creative, unwind, and have fun.
events.blurb: Adults make their own jewelry using provided supplies and project ideas at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Game On at the Library
events.description: Play board games at the Joyce Ellington Branch every Sunday at 1:00 p.m. Choose from a large selection of new and classic games for all ages. Bring your family and friends, roll the dice, and enjoy some friendly competition! No registration required.
events.blurb: Choose from a large selection of board games and play with family and friends at the library.

events.title: Explore Human Anatomy with AnatoKidz
events.description: Explore how the human body works through interactive lessons and activities! Learn about the brain, heart, lungs, bones, and more while building curiosity, confidence, and critical thinking skills. This free, two-part series is recommended for children ages 5 to 10. Attend one or both sessions. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn how the brain, heart, lungs, and bones work through interactive lessons and activities in a free series for kids ages 5 to 10.

events.title: Nameless Anime Club
events.description: Do you enjoy anime and manga? Join Edenvale Branch Library's Nameless Anime Club every fourth Sunday of the month! Watch classic anime and newer series while making new friends! Participants are welcome to drop in anytime during our program. We hope to see you there! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Drop in to watch classic and current anime episodes and meet other fans at Edenvale Library.

events.title: Journey of finding geodes
events.description: Geodes are as beautiful and diverse as the areas they are found in. Silicon Valley Gem and Mineral Society veteran Steve May will talk about geode formations, how to plan a trip as well as what tools and permits you will need. Join us for a lively discussion. Bring your questions. A Q&A will follow the presentation.
events.blurb: Hear Silicon Valley Gem and Mineral Society veteran Steve May talk geode formation, trip planning, tools and permits, then ask questions.

events.title: Board Game Zone

events.blurb: Play board games from a large selection of new and classic titles at Seven Trees Library, with no registration required.

events.title: Music & Storytelling with Kirk Waller
events.description: Join us for a performance with musician and storyteller Kirk Waller! Kirk mesmerizes audiences of all ages with a dynamic blend of music, movement, and storytelling. Journey with him through captivating tales from long ago and far away, brought vividly to life through his energetic and engaging performance style.
events.blurb: Watch musician and storyteller Kirk Waller mix music, movement, and stories in a performance for audiences of all ages.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Optimizing Social Security Benefits
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a workshop series on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada explain strategies for optimizing your Social Security benefits.

events.title: Excel Basics
events.description: New to Microsoft Excel? This beginner-friendly workshop will introduce you to the essentials, including navigating spreadsheets, entering and formatting data, creating simple formulas, and organizing information. Get comfortable with Excel and build the skills you need to confidently tackle everyday tasks. Free.
events.blurb: Learn to navigate spreadsheets, enter data, and build simple formulas in this beginner Excel workshop.

events.title: Jewelry Making: STEM Craft
events.description: Be a Mini Maker! Join us for a creative jewelry making craft workshop. Learn how to design and create your own unique bracelet using colorful beads and charms, and take home your very own beaded bracelet. Materials will be provided. Recommended for ages 7 and up. Perfect for beginners and experienced crafters!
events.blurb: Design and string your own beaded bracelet with charms in this STEM-themed jewelry making craft session.

events.title: Tai Chi for Seniors
events.description: Join us at Dr. Roberto Cruz Alum Rock Library for an hour of Tai Chi exercises. Tai Chi improves strength, flexibility, aerobic conditioning, and balance. It's been proven to improve cardiovascular fitness, lower blood pressure, prevent falls, and help people who have arthritis. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Move through an hour of Tai Chi exercises aimed at strength, flexibility, balance, and aerobic conditioning, in a class for seniors.

events.title: STEM: Lotus Pond Origami Workshop
events.description: Practice geometry, fractions, and sequential reasoning through folding origami lotuses. This program is recommended for patrons aged 6-11. Registration required; if you are registered, please arrive on time. Registrants who are more than 15 minutes late may lose their registered spot to a walk-in participant.
events.blurb: Fold origami lotuses while practicing geometry, fractions, and sequential reasoning in a STEM workshop for kids aged 6-11 at Berryessa Library.

events.title: Sounds of South Asia: an Exhibit
events.description: This interactive photography exhibit showcases several musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent. Each exhibit will have a QR code that allows participants to listen to the sound of the instruments played in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. They include stringed, wind, and percussion instruments passed down through generations, which are still played around the Bay Area. Come and enjoy this exhibit, which starts on November 14, 2026, and closes on December 5, 2026. The exhibit is brought to you by the South Asians in Silicon Valley initiative at the SJSU King Library. Through this unique initiative, the SJSU King Library records, preserves, and shares the living legacy of the South Asian diaspora in the San Francisco Bay Area. Website: https://library.sjsu.edu/sasv
events.blurb: See an interactive photography exhibit featuring musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent.

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!); Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Celebrate Diwali with the community at Mitchell Park Community Center's Festival of Lights.

events.title: Volunteer in the Historic Orchard with UC Master Gardeners!
events.description: The Historic Orchard is a 3.3-acre site planted in 1994 and located in Guadalupe Gardens just south of Taylor Street, adjacent to the Heritage Rose Garden and River Park trails. In the 1930s and '40s, almost everyone who lived here was engaged in the business of fruit production: growing, picking, packing, canning, selling, or otherwise supporting the industry. Today, with very few orchards remaining, this is a place where adults and children can come to experience a piece of local history. Fruit harvested from the Historic Orchard is donated to Second Harvest of Silicon Valley and local shelters. Help us maintain the River Park's Historic Orchard with activities including tree planting and pruning; disease diagnosis and treatment; sun scald prevention painting; sheet mulching; experimenting with different types of irrigation or ground cover; and grafting for improved pollination. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Restrooms are available at the Rotary Play Garden and will require staff assistance. events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
